title: Rhythm Comb
concept: Base A intensified — 12 ticks clustered in irregular groups so the rhythm itself, not just three gaps, reads as variable; the three tallest ticks carry the Julia dots.
why: The most literal refinement of the hero motif you chose; scales density up without losing the baseline-and-ticks read.
risk: Busiest of the set; at 32px the filler ticks fuzz into a grey band (the three dots still pop).
top3_reason: It's the direct, stronger evolution of the exact mark you already picked (Base A) — the standalone 'symbol' of the system. Crop it for social/app icons; drop to comb-08 for a true 16–32px favicon.

title: Cycle Ring
motif: comb bent into a full ring
concept: The comb bent into a full ring — ticks radiate from a circle at irregular angular gaps (a cyclic cardiac cycle); three extended ticks carry the Julia dots.
why: The most distinctive silhouette in the set (radial vs linear) and reads well as an app icon at any size.
risk: Could look clock-like; mitigated by irregular (non-12-hour) spacing and the dot colors.

title: Minimal Gaps
concept: Stripped to three large Julia dots on a barely-there baseline with two small caliper marks making the unequal gaps explicit — the comb fully implied.
why: Cleanest of the set and the best true favicon: nothing is lost in downscaling (verified crisp at 32px).
risk: Loses the comb texture that makes Base A distinctive; reads generic if the caliper marks are removed.

title: Tachogram
concept: Classic tachogram — beat number on x, interval duration as point height on y, points joined by a step line; three enlarged colored points anchor identity among grey ones.
why: The most 'real HRV analysis output' of the set — anyone who's plotted NN-intervals recognizes it instantly.
risk: The zig-zag could brush 'ECG' if too spiky; kept rounded and modest (whitelisted IBI vocabulary).

title: Interval Calipers
concept: Three beat-dots on the baseline; two engineering-style dimension brackets span beat1→2 and beat2→3 at different lengths, explicitly measuring the unequal IBI gaps.
why: The most explicit 'this measures a duration' read — good where the measurement idea must be instant.
risk: Could be mistaken for a bar-chart/table icon if colors are stripped.

title: Floating Beats
motif: event markers over a plain raster
concept: A regular tick timeline underneath with three Julia dots floating above at irregular heights, each linked by a thin dashed stem — the floating heights are the variability signal.
why: Cleanly separates 'when' (regular raster) from 'how variable' (floating heights) — a distinct two-layer composition.
risk: Dashed stems can vanish at 32px (the floating dots still read as the hero).

title: Poincaré
concept: NN(n) vs NN(n+1) scatter — axes, a 45° diagonal, grey interval-pairs inside a faint SD1/SD2 ellipse on the diagonal, with three colored anchor points.
why: Signals analytical depth (a real HRV metric plot) and is visually the most distinctive 'documentation' companion mark.
risk: Most detail-heavy icon; axis lines and scatter thin out at 32px — bump size if used very small.

title: Cardiac Arc
concept: The comb bent along a gentle upward arc — one cycle read left-to-right along a curve; ticks radiate outward and three carry the Julia dots.
why: Softens the motif (less 'ruler', more 'pulse') and reads well as a badge/favicon silhouette.
risk: Faint resemblance to a crown/rainbow at a glance; dot colors and tick texture disambiguate.

title: Interval Barcode
concept: Only vertical bars packed edge to edge — bar width encodes IBI duration; most are grey, three are purple/red/green standing in for the identity beats.
why: The boldest, most brandable icon; reads as a 'waveform of durations' rather than any ECG shape.
risk: Deliberately has no circular dots — identity is carried by bar color, not dots (flag if reviewers expect circles).

title: Vertical Raster
concept: The comb rotated 90° — a vertical baseline with horizontal ticks stacked at irregular vertical spacing; three ticks extend to the Julia dots.
why: A useful alternate orientation for sidebar/vertical-nav icon slots.
risk: Less immediately 'cardiac' than the horizontal version; the raster read needs the dots to anchor it.

title: Underlined by the Comb
concept: No separate icon block — the whole 'HeartRateLab' wordmark is underlined by an irregular IBI tick comb; three ticks in the Julia colors are dot-capped, echoing identity inline with the type.
why: The strongest type-led option; the comb underline scans as a data-signature rather than decoration.
risk: At small sizes the underline ticks can merge into a solid rule — best at medium+ (favicon should fall back to an icon-only mark).
top3_reason: My overall favorite. It fuses both things you liked — the IBI comb and the name lockup — into one mark: the package name literally written onto an inter-beat recording. Distinctive, legible, and unmistakably about interval variability.

title: Tick-Comb Mini
concept: Three colored ticks at unequal spacing and heights (= unequal IBI durations), each capped with a small Julia dot — a compact, icon-first version of Base A's comb, set left of the wordmark.
why: Ties directly to the hero comb while staying a clean 'icon + name' lockup — the format you said you liked.
risk: At very small sizes the dot caps can fuse with the ticks; keep dot radius ≥ stroke width.
top3_reason: The horizontal 'logo next to the name' you specifically liked — but rebuilt honestly: a tiny IBI comb instead of the ECG spike. This is the everyday workhorse lockup for README headers and docs.

title: Measured Gap
concept: Three dot-beats on a timeline plus a small caliper explicitly measuring the interval between the last two beats — the 'we measure intervals' story made literal, beside the wordmark.
why: The caliper is unambiguous — nobody could mistake this for a heartbeat monitor.
risk: The caliper is small at icon scale; needs thicker strokes below ~64px stand-alone.

title: Triad on the Timeline
concept: The three Julia dots sit directly on a plain baseline with visibly unequal gaps — the gaps are the inter-beat intervals, no waveform involved — beside the wordmark.
why: The most legible/neutral option; reads instantly as 'events on a line' — a safe default lockup.
risk: Low risk; can look generic if not seen alongside the tick-comb variants.

title: Comb Stack
concept: Stacked lockup — Base A's full tick-comb icon (grey ticks + three dot-capped colored ticks) centered above the wordmark.
why: The most faithful port of the Base A hero icon into a lockup — best if you want one lockup that matches the standalone icon exactly.
risk: None major; verify icon/word vertical rhythm at target sizes.

title: Heart·Rate·Lab
concept: 'Rate' is set larger and in Julia red for emphasis (the product's core subject), paired with a tiny 3-tick dot-capped comb at left.
why: The weighted 'Rate' is a memorable reading aid tying the accent color to the product's central concept.
risk: Three text runs must stay baseline-aligned if re-flowed/localized; keep as one composed unit.

title: Triad Stack (Tight)
concept: Stacked lockup — triad on a plain timeline (larger dots, unequal gaps) above a tightly tracked wordmark.
why: Big dots read well even at small stacked-icon crops; tight tracking gives a modern condensed feel.
risk: Tight tracking pushes legibility slightly; don't set textLength smaller.

title: Big Icon, Wide Track
concept: A larger triad-on-timeline icon with a caliper under the last gap, paired with a looser-tracked wordmark on a slightly raised baseline — a scale/alignment study.
why: Shows the lockup scaling gracefully with a dominant icon — useful for hero/splash placements.
risk: The raised text baseline is a subtle asymmetry; don't mix with the centered lockups in one UI.

title: Accented Heart
motif: three dots as a type accent
concept: A small triad of dots sits as an accent/tittle above the 'a' in 'Heart' — the three Julia dots become a type-level detail rather than a separate icon.
why: The most minimal/sophisticated option — no icon 'box', just a knowing detail for people who look twice.
risk: The accent is subtle; at very small sizes it can read as noise on the glyph — medium-to-large use only.

title: Compact Fused Mark
concept: Three small unequal-spaced beat-dots tucked under-left on a short baseline, sitting close to and almost fusing with the wordmark — the tightest horizontal lockup.
why: The smallest footprint of the horizontal set — best for tight UI chrome (navbars, README badges).
risk: The dots are small (r≈15–17); keep a minimum render width (~200px) to preserve the Julia-dot identity.

title: Comb Underline
concept: The plain rule under the wordmark is replaced by the actual IBI comb — irregular ticks on a baseline, three dot-capped — so the underline itself is the beat raster.
why: The closest 1:1 reuse of Base A's own vocabulary; instantly reads as 'comb become underline', very on-brief.
risk: The underline could be mistaken for decoration if scaled too small; keep dot caps visible.

title: Cyclic Beat Arc
motif: comb bent into an arc + dots
concept: The comb is bent into a shallow arc above the name (a cyclic beat); irregular ticks radiate off it and the three Julia dots sit on the arc at unequal angular spacing.
why: The most distinctive silhouette of the combos — reads as a badge/seal from a distance while resolving into comb+dots up close.
risk: The arc must not be mistaken for a waveform; radiating ticks kept straight to avoid an ECG-adjacent read.

title: Beat Timeline
concept: The three Julia dots sit on a timeline under the wordmark with clearly unequal gaps (plus a few minor ticks) — the timeline is the hero, the dots are beat events in time.
why: The most literal expression of 'IBI' — the variable gap is the message; a very clean, calm composition.
risk: Can read as 'just 3 dots on a line' without the minor ticks; keep some comb texture.

title: Interval Ruler
concept: A thin ruler runs under the single wordmark with three colored caliper marks at the syllable boundaries (Heart|Rate|Lab) — measuring the word itself like a sequence of intervals.
why: Turns the wordmark into the 'signal being measured' — a clever literal fusion of typography and IBI measurement.
risk: Subtler than a literal comb; benefits from context on first exposure (docs/README).

title: Stacked Comb + Name
concept: A compact vertical lockup — the IBI comb icon (near-verbatim Base A, scaled) above, the wordmark centered below.
why: The most traditional 'icon + name' structure — a compact app-icon-adjacent lockup for square avatars.
risk: The least 'invented' fusion — more juxtaposition than fusion (kept per the brief's stacked requirement).

title: Stacked Tachogram
concept: A tachogram (bar heights = interval durations, three colored by the triad) sits above the wordmark in a compact vertical lockup.
why: Introduces a second IBI vocabulary (bars, not ticks) into the stacked format — real variety versus combo-06.
risk: Bars can look like a generic analytics chart if muted; keep the three triad bars saturated.

title: Diacritic Triad
concept: The three Julia dots perch above the H, R and L like diacritics on the wordmark's ascenders; a plain grey comb runs beneath the word as the 'beat floor'.
why: The most typographic fusion — the triad becomes part of the letterforms while the comb carries IBI honesty.
risk: Dot alignment over H/R/L is font-metric-approximate; verify at final render.

title: Ticks Rising Into the Triad
concept: A sparse row of minor grey ticks sits above the name; three grow tall and terminate in the Julia dots, so the triad reads as the comb's peaks floating over the wordmark.
why: Inverts combo-01's placement (comb above, not below), giving variety while reusing the honest ticks+dots language.
risk: At small sizes the thin grey ticks may disappear, leaving three isolated dots.

title: Three Syllable Combs
concept: Three small mini-combs (each with a dot-capped tall tick) sit under Heart·Rate·Lab on one shared baseline — the comb distributed under the word rather than concentrated.
why: Ties each Julia-color dot to a syllable, reinforcing 'Heart-Rate-Lab' as three linked ideas under one timeline.
risk: Per-glyph alignment depends on font metrics; ticks may drift slightly off-syllable on other engines.

title: Tachogram Baseplate
concept: The tachogram bars run directly under the full-width wordmark like a textured baseplate/EQ meter — one continuous horizontal mark.
why: Completes the set's coverage of all allowed IBI motifs in horizontal form; reads well small since bars are chunky.
risk: At very small sizes the thin bars blur together; reduce bar count for a favicon variant.
